scenes.title: Hook: A Plant Making Its Own Dinner
scenes.say: Plants do not eat food the way we do. Yet every leaf on a tree is busy making its own food. Let us find out how.
scenes.visual: A potted plant centred on a plain chalk-white background. A small sun drawn in the top left corner with a few short chalk rays. Soft chalk arrows dance around the leaves to suggest activity. Title text fades in: Photosynthesis.

scenes.title: What Goes In
scenes.say: Photosynthesis needs three ingredients. Carbon dioxide from the air. Water from the soil. And light energy from the sun.
scenes.visual: A simple leaf diagram drawn with a few curved shapes and a midrib line. Three labelled arrows point toward the leaf: an arrow from the air labelled carbon dioxide, an arrow from below labelled water, and a yellow sun ray labelled light. Each label appears one after another as it is spoken.

scenes.title: Inside the Leaf
scenes.say: Inside the leaf are tiny green parts called chloroplasts. They contain chlorophyll, which captures the light energy the plant needs.
scenes.visual: A zoomed-in circle of the leaf cell drawn with a simple oval outline. Several small green ovals inside are labelled chloroplast. A short chalk label reads chlorophyll captures light. Light rays drawn as dashed yellow lines strike the green shapes.

scenes.title: What Comes Out
scenes.say: Using that light energy, the plant turns carbon dioxide and water into glucose, a sugar used for energy. It also releases oxygen into the air.
scenes.visual: The leaf diagram returns. Arrows now point out: one arrow labelled glucose leaves the leaf, and another arrow labelled oxygen floats up into the air. The word equation is written across the bottom in chalk.

scenes.title: The Word Equation
scenes.say: Here is the word equation. Carbon dioxide plus water, in the presence of light and chlorophyll, gives glucose plus oxygen.
scenes.visual: Chalk text line by line: carbon dioxide plus water, then an arrow with light and chlorophyll written above it, then glucose plus oxygen. Each reactant and product is underlined in a different chalk colour as it is read.

scenes.title: Practice Question
scenes.say: Practice question. Which gas does a plant take in from the air during photosynthesis? Pause the video and think. The answer is carbon dioxide.
scenes.visual: A chalk-boxed question on the screen: Which gas does a plant take in from the air during photosynthesis? A pause symbol appears, then the answer carbon dioxide is revealed with a chalk circle drawn around it.
